equity_bridge.note: FY2026 10-K balance sheet, 30-Jun-2026; flows are consolidated so NCI is charged once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (3.1%), cross-checked against revenue 5yr (2.7%) and EPS 5yr (3.5%); rounded to 3.0% as the mid-horizon base growth rate, with FY2027 anchored to guidance (1-3%) instead
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC) FY2021 $15,044M -> FY2023 $13,241M -> FY2026 $14,623M. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR is slightly negative because FY2021 was a pandemic-demand/working-capital peak ($15.6B reported FCF on $76B revenue, 20.5% margin); the 3yr figure (+3.4%) is the better read. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.2pp of each other: SBC is ~0.6% of revenue and is not growing faster than cash flow. Equity CAGR diverges by <30% from revenue and EPS; no flag. Equity is a weak growth anchor for PG because ~$15B/yr is returned via dividends and buybacks.

scenario_narratives.base: Steady-state staples compounder: 2-3% revenue growth, margin recovers to slightly above the FY2025 pre-restructuring level as the Portfolio & Productivity program completes in FY2027, capex normalises to 4.5%, and ~$15-17B/yr of owner FCF is returned through a 68-year dividend record and buybacks. Axes watched: organic volume vs price/mix split, gross margin vs the ~$1B FY27 cost headwind, restructuring savings reaching the P&L.
scenario_narratives.bull: Volume re-acceleration plus restructuring delivery: 4% organic growth through FY2031 with the pre-SBC EBITDA margin stepping to 30% as tariffs/commodities ease and overhead comes out; Health Care and premium Beauty mix lift continue.
scenario_narratives.bear: Premium-pricing model under trade-down pressure: growth capped at ~2%, China a persistent drag, cost headwinds absorbed in margin, restructuring savings reinvested in price; the stock de-rates toward a 2%-grower multiple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF (SBC fully expensed, share count flat) on a mature, non-cyclical staples compounder. The value is almost entirely the terminal value of a 2.5-3% grower at a 20x FCF cap; the single biggest input is the discount rate, and PG trades at ~25x owner FCF today versus the model's 20x cap. Scenario weights are tilted toward the bear because the current data (1% organic growth, cost headwinds) describe it better than the bull.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal-value dominated: ~70%+ of EV sits in the terminal, and the valuation moves ~10% per 50bps of WACC.
The 20x FCF cap binds in every scenario; the market currently pays ~25x, so the model embeds a de-rating relative to today's multiple.
Margin path assumes the FY2026-27 restructuring charges ($1.5-2.0B pre-tax) are finite and do not recur; PG has run restructuring programs almost continuously since 2012.
Diluted share count includes the convertible ESOP preferred; dividends on that preferred (~$250M/yr) are treated as common distributions, not debt service.
Tariff and commodity costs: a further $1B swing is ~1.1% of revenue, i.e. roughly one scenario-step of margin.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 137.62-167.25.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 80424): FY2026 10-K (year ended 30-Jun-2026) for revenue, operating income, D&A, SBC, capex, OCF, cash, debt, NCI, cash taxes, buybacks; PG_Metrics.csv (105 periods) for history.
data_sources.qualitative: PG_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): FY2027 guidance (sales +1-3%, core EPS flat to +3%, ~$1B after-tax cost headwind), Portfolio & Productivity restructuring, CEO transition, bull/bear points.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 2,324.4M basic shares on the FY2026 10-K cover (31-Jul-2026) plus the FY2026 diluted-minus-basic spread of 88.8M (weighted diluted 2,422.5M less weighted basic 2,333.7M: stock options/RSUs and the convertible Class A ESOP preferred). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income was $430M (XBRL InvestmentIncomeInterest) but PG carries $24.2B of NET DEBT, so the cash pile is not added to EV and interest income is NOT stripped from owner FCF (rule: strip only when net cash is material).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement, ShareBasedCompensation $524M (XBRL). PG does not tag a separate net-share-settlement tax withholding line (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation absent); PG settles mostly via option exercises (FY26 proceeds $920M), so the add-back is used as the full SBC charge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $5,028M (FY2025 $6,500M). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded in cash, and buybacks have run at ~10x the SBC charge, so the flat-count convention is conservative for PG.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.55 for a mega-cap staple gives a cost of equity ~6.9%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (FY26 interest paid $866M on ~$34B), ~3.5% after tax; debt ~9% of capital (EV ~$371B). Blended WACC ~6.6%, rounded UP to 7.0% as the house base. The same 7.0% is used in every scenario; risk is carried in the scenario weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases ($887M liability at 30-Jun-2026) are expensed inside operating income and paid through operating cash flow, so the lease cost already sits in EBITDA and FCF. No lease liability added to net debt and no separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path = 0): one treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is immaterial ($230M book, $98M of FY26 net income). Flows are consolidated; the NCI is deducted once at book value in the equity bridge.
inputs.tax_note: FY2026 cash taxes paid $4,678M on pre-tax income $20,377M = 23.0%; GAAP provision 20.8%. The engine applies the cash rate to EBIT (which is pre-interest, so the rate on EBIT is slightly lower): 22.5% held flat. No NOLs, credits or valuation-allowance releases to ramp.
inputs.ebitda_basis: CSV EBITDA (FY26 $22,908M = operating income $19,748M + D&A $3,160M) is AFTER the $524M SBC expense and AFTER $1,230M of restructuring charges. The engine's ebitda_margin_path is the PRE-SBC margin (FY26 = 26.9% = (22,908+524)/87,032), with SBC then charged via sbc_pct_path. FY25 pre-SBC margin was 28.2%; FY26 is depressed ~140bps by restructuring charges that roll off after FY2027.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF on the component route (make build-dcf), scenario-weighted. PG is a US-listed, USD-reporting, non-cyclical consumer staples operating company, so the routing table's first row applies and none of the owner-fcf-adaptations (currency, leases under IFRS-16, NCI, SBC-zero, cyclical mid-cycling) are needed; FY2026 is not a cyclical trough or peak (organic growth ~1%, margin dented by a disclosed, finite restructuring program). Owner FCF FY26 = reported FCF 15,147 - SBC 524 = 14,623 (interest income not stripped: net-debt company). Price is the 2026-10-01 regular close (not after-hours). Net debt and share count are from the FY2026 10-K (balance sheet 30-Jun-2026, cover shares 31-Jul-2026), the latest filing; Q1 FY2027 (30-Sep-2026) has not been filed yet. Horizon 10 years so the terminal year capitalises a matured post-restructuring margin.

bear.narrative: Private-label and value-brand trade-down bites in developed markets and Greater China stays weak, so FY2027 lands at the bottom of guidance (+0.5%) and growth never gets past 2% (price/mix with flat-to-down volume). Tariff and commodity headwinds (~$1B after-tax in FY2027) outrun productivity, the restructuring savings are reinvested in price rather than reaching the margin, and pre-SBC EBITDA settles at 26% (60bps below the restructuring-depressed FY2026 level). Capex stays at 5%, no working-capital help. Terminal 2.0%, 18x cap (the market will not pay a 20x multiple for a 2% grower); Gordon at 7%/2% gives 20.4x so the cap binds.

base.narrative: FY2027 revenue +2% (midpoint of 1-3% guidance); thereafter 3%/yr (the pre-2020 'GDP-plus' algorithm of ~1-2% volume plus ~1-2% price/mix) fading to 2.5% by year 9. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 27.2% in FY2027 (remaining restructuring charges and the ~$1B after-tax input-cost headwind net of productivity, GAAP margin up slightly on lower restructuring) rising to 28.5% by FY2030 as the Portfolio & Productivity program completes -- that is only ~30bps above the FY2025 pre-restructuring level, not a step-change. D&A 3.6%->3.5%, capex 4.9%->4.5% of revenue (FY26 capex 5.1% was an elevated supply-chain year; PG's long-run range is 4-5%), cash tax 22.5%, 5% working-capital capture (PG runs negative working capital, so growth releases a little cash). Terminal 2.5% growth at 7% WACC; the 20x cap binds (Gordon would give 22.8x).

bull.narrative: Volume growth re-accelerates (Q3 FY26 was the first organic volume growth in a year) and holds with price/mix for 4% top-line through FY2031; restructuring delivers a genuine 150bps margin step (pre-SBC EBITDA to 30%, roughly where FY2021's pandemic peak sat) as tariffs/commodities ease and 7,000 overhead roles come out; capex settles at 4.3%. Terminal 3.0%, same 7% WACC; 20x cap binds.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25% and bull cut from 35% to 25%. PG has no solvency or refinancing risk (AA- credit, 24x interest cover) so the bear is a margin/growth case, not a survival case -- but its axes are live today: FY2026 organic growth was ~1%, Q4 FY26 missed on revenue, gross margin fell 100bps, and management has guided a ~$1B after-tax cost headwind for FY2027. The bull case needs two independent things to go right (volume re-acceleration AND restructuring savings reaching the margin rather than being reinvested) during a CEO transition, so it does not merit 35%. Base case 50% as the house default.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
